preconditions.description: The number of vectors n and dimensions m are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= k <= 2 for k in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in input_lines[1:]])
preconditions.description: Each vector description starts with an integer k (1 or 2) indicating the number of 1s.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= x <= m for x in coords) and len(coords) == k for k, coords in [(int(line.split()[0]), [int(x) for x in line.split()[1:]]) for line in input_lines[1:]])
preconditions.description: The coordinates for each vector are distinct integers between 1 and m, matching the count k.

preconditions.expression: len(set(tuple(sorted([int(x) for x in line.split()[1:]])) for line in input_lines[1:])) == n
preconditions.description: All n vectors in the input are distinct.

postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly two lines.
The first line contains exactly two integers.
The first integer is the size of the span T modulo 10^9+7, where rank is the dimension of the subspace spanned by the selected vectors.
The second integer is the size of the minimal subset S'.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines[1].split()) == len(selected_indices) if len(selected_indices) > 0 else True
postconditions.description: The second line contains the indices of the selected vectors, matching the count in the first line.
The output indices are in ascending order.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= idx <= n for idx in selected_indices)
postconditions.description: All output indices are valid 1-based indices from the input.
The number of selected vectors equals the rank of the vector space spanned by S.
The selected vectors span the same subspace as the original set S.
Among all minimal subsets of S that span T, the selected indices form the lexicographically smallest set.
